chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Sulayman ibn Khalid who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the hunted prey that its owner finds — may he eat it? He said: If he knows that it was his shooting which killed it, then let him eat.

key_terms.الرَّمِيَّة: The hunted game; prey that has been shot at — specifically an animal shot with an arrow or projectile
key_terms.رَمْيَتُه: His shooting/shot; the act of throwing or shooting by the hunter
key_terms.فَلْيَأْكُلْ: Permissive imperative: 'let him eat' — a ruling that it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat hunted game if you find it dead after shooting it?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a specific jurisprudential scenario in hunting: a hunter who shot at an animal but only finds the dead prey later. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) rules that the meat is permissible to eat only if the hunter has certainty (not mere probability) that his own shot was the cause of death. This ruling reflects the Islamic principle that certainty of lawful slaughter is required for meat to be halal, especially in hunting where the animal may have died from another cause.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al nazar Bin Suweyd, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Suleyman Bin Khalid who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the (prey) shot at, its owner finds it, can he eat it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If he knew that it was his shooting which killed it, so let him eat’.
en.sarwar: 7. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Hisham ibn Salim from Sulayman ibn Khalid who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a prey that its owner finds; if he can use it for food.
He (the Imam) said, ’If he knows that it is his shot that has killed it, he can use it for food.’”
